Long-form is about 37 views and 2.7 watch hours a day. At that pace YPP is about 4 years away. Feb 2027 needs about 33 h a day (12×), and the 800 h November target can't be reached.

8 of 21 Shorts were held: 5 for music masking, 1 for a CTA naming a video we couldn't confirm live. Carousels still reach 0–4.
This week: practical tirzepatide long-forms by default, plus fresh news only when it has a headline number. "What Is [drug]?" explainers are paused. Spoken CTAs no longer name video titles.

bottleneck:
The bottleneck is long-form reach. Watch time per viewer isn't the problem: GLP-1 long-forms hold a median AVD of about 265 s, and the practical tirzepatide ones hold 35–53%. What's missing is people arriving. Today we get about 37 long-form views and 2.7 watch hours a day, against the roughly 33 h a day that YPP by Feb 2027 needs. What cost the most this week:
(1) Topic choice. 4 of 6 logged long-forms went to lanes that don't pull: pharmacy (8 views, 20 min), Medicare (7, 0 min), the bare "What Is Petrelintide?" explainer (4 at day 2) and the elecoglipron explainer (not logged yet). Across our history, broad head-term titles also lose to big channels: "Tirzepatide vs Semaglutide…" got 9 views even though its Short got 163. The 3 practical tirzepatide videos (How Long 37 views/122 min, What to Eat 24/39, Side Effects 23/53) earned 91% of the week's new watch minutes. Strength Training is still climbing (48 at day 9, 70 at day 11).
(2) No path from Shorts to long-form. 10,513 Shorts views in 90 days have produced no measurable long-form traffic. No Short has had a working link yet, there are no end screens or related-video links, and spoken CTAs naming unconfirmed titles caused a hold (S3 10-26) and line-1 misses.
(3) Production waste. 8 of 21 Shorts were held (5 for masking at 0.034–0.039, while long-forms mix at 0.003–0.018). About 7 carousels a week reach 0–4.
(4) We still can't see impressions, CTR or traffic sources, so we can't tell whether packaging or discovery is failing. 10-26 and lane labels aren't logged.
playbook_markdown:
# InforMed growth playbook: week of 2026-10-28

**Status: off track.** 45 of 4,000 watch hours (1.1%); 373 of 1,000 subs. Long-form median this week: 15.5 views (target 30+). Practical tirzepatide long-forms earned 91% of this week's new watch minutes. Every long-form slot goes to what earns minutes.

## Long-form (1 a day, 14:00 ET, 8–12 min)
1. **Lane C, fresh result (Exp C).** All of these must hold:
   - The result first became public within 48 h (check the first-report date).
   - It's a named next-gen drug, with a headline efficacy number from a randomized trial.
   - Best case: a tirzepatide or semaglutide arm, like EloraTZP.
   - Filings, Phase 1, food-effect or status-only news go to a Short instead.
   - Drug name first in the title. Label it `lane: C`.
2. **Lane A, practical tirzepatide (Exp A). The default on every other day.** This week, in this order:
   - "Tirzepatide and Your Bones and Muscle: What the Evidence Says". This is an allowed exception to the 14-day Short-repeat rule.
   - "Protein on Tirzepatide: How Much and Why"
   - "What Happens When You Stop Tirzepatide?" Use SURMOUNT-4 and say "don't stop or change your medicine on your own".
   - "Tirzepatide Hair Loss: How Common Is It and What Helps?"
   - "Tirzepatide Weight Loss Plateau: What the Trials Show"
   - Label each one `lane: A`.
- **Paused:** Lane P "What Is [drug]?" explainers (petrelintide had 4 views at day 2). This will be reviewed at day 7 for petrelintide and elecoglipron.
- **Banned in long-form:**
  - Cost, coverage, Medicare, pharmacy and gray-market topics.
  - Single-trial deep dives on approved drugs.
  - Timeline-only topics.
  - "Did X beat Y?" without a randomized head-to-head trial.
  - Broad head-term titles that big channels own (e.g. "Tirzepatide vs Semaglutide": 9 views).

## Long-form packaging and retention
- **Title:** the long-tail question a tirzepatide user would type, drug name first, about 60 characters or fewer, at most 1 number. It must be fully paid off in the video.
- **Thumbnail:** 4 words or fewer, never repeating the title. One labelled character, one honest emotion.
- **0–15 s:** open on a concrete "you" scenario and give the first answer. No trial-number openings and no setup.
- **Body:** re-hook every 45–75 s. Name chapters after searched questions. One subscribe ask, after the payoff.
- **Ending (new):** don't speak any video title. Say "Watch next: the video on screen now, linked at the top of the description." The publisher adds the verified "▶ Watch next" link, and the owner adds the end screen.

## Shorts (3 a day, at most 170 words, 60–85 s)
- **08:00, body worry:** a calm "honest uncertainty" Short (gallbladder, pancreas, hair, bone density, muscle). Tirzepatide in the title where the evidence covers it. It wins on both YouTube and Instagram.
- **13:00, lead.** Pick one:
  - a two-drug head-to-head with tirzepatide named first and a new trial each time;
  - a retatrutide Short with new Phase 3 data or a "what's confirmed?" fact, with a loop ending;
  - a gray-market "what's confirmed?" Short with a new dated FDA/MHRA/manufacturer fact (at most 1 a week).
- **20:00, funnel Short (Exp D, unchanged):** a fresh single question answered by a live long-form. Rotate: that day's Lane C video, then EloraTZP, then Strength Training on Tirzepatide.
  - Last spoken line: "Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description."
  - The publisher writes all links. Agents never write YouTube URLs or spoken titles.
- **Banned:**
  - "Is X approved yet?" titles.
  - "3 Ways…" lists.
  - Brand-first titles, and semaglutide-only titles (unless the evidence is semaglutide-only).
  - Cost or coverage Shorts.
  - Observational surgery angles.
  - Titles that name no drug.
  - Scare framing.
- **Variety:** any one trial in at most 1 Short a week, no back-to-back same-template titles, a new fact in every piece.

## Quality gates (non-negotiable)
- **Masking:** Shorts mix at 0.02 or lower the first time, at the long-form music level. Measure last. Above 0.03 is an automatic drop: 5 Shorts were lost this week.
- **Captions:** built from on-screen text. Numbers match their stat pills exactly; never split a number or trial name.
- **Safety lines:** every piece carries "Not personal advice" and "talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you". No dosing, switching or stopping advice, and no compounded or online sources. The fact-checker and the Editor-in-Chief always win.

## Carousels (until the owner decides)
- Reuse verified Short text only, with zero new research.

## Experiments (log `lane` in every long-form's metadata)
- **Exp A:** Lane A on every day without qualifying news. Score views and watch minutes at day 7 and day 28. Call it at n=8 (about 11-03).
- **Exp C:** only qualifying news days. Score day-7 views against the median of 24. Success: a median of 50 or more at n=4.
- **Exp D:** every 20:00 Short. The analyst logs the target long-form's viewCount for the 3 days before and after each one. Call it at n=6 Shorts with a verified link.
- **Hold constant:** 14:00 ET, 8–12 min, the same retention rules.

experiments.name: Exp A: Practical tirzepatide long-forms (Lane A)
experiments.hypothesis: Practical, long-tail tirzepatide questions people search (strength training, protein, side effects, stopping) beat approved-drug deep dives (median 8–17) and keep gaining views over time.
experiments.change: Lane A runs on every day without qualifying Lane C news (Lane P is paused). Practical tirzepatide topics only, long-tail searched question first, about 60 characters or fewer, at most 1 number. Cost, coverage and timeline-only topics are excluded. Slot, length and retention rules stay the same.
experiments.metric: Views and watch minutes at day 7 and day 28. Success: day-7 median views of 25 or more and watch-minute median of 60 or more, still growing at day 28.
experiments.min_sample: n=8 videos (expected about 11-03). Judge each video at day 7 and day 28.
experiments.result: Interim signal, on target so far. In-window in-lane videos (n=3): How Long 37 views/122 min, What to Eat 24/39, Side Effects 23/53 (day 3). Adding Strength Training (70/129, still climbing: 48 at day 9, 70 at day 11) gives n=4: median 30.5 views and about 88 min. These earned 91% of this week's new long-form watch minutes. Medicare (7 views, 0 min) is excluded as a cost topic.

experiments.name: Exp B: Gray-market 'what's actually confirmed' long-forms
experiments.hypothesis: Our strongest Short lane (gray-market 'what's confirmed?', median about 105, n=7) would also work as long-form.
experiments.change: 2 long-forms a week in lane B, credited and dated, no sellers named.
experiments.metric: Day-7 views compared with the GLP-1 long-form median. Success: day-7 median of 33 or more.
experiments.result: Closed early at n=1. The pharmacy check got 8 views and 20 min. That's an anecdote, not proof the lane fails. We closed it because of the opportunity cost against Lane A and because the lane sits close to the 'online sources' policy line. Gray-market stays Shorts-only, at most 1 a week.

experiments.name: Exp C: First explainer within 48 h of a new named result
experiments.hypothesis: Being the first clear explainer of a newly public, named trial result with a headline number (ideally against tirzepatide or semaglutide) drives far more long-form views than evergreen topics (EloraTZP 575 views, 1,474 min).
experiments.change: Tightened: the long-form slot goes to the news only when all of these hold. The result first became public within 48 h. It's a named next-gen drug. It has a headline efficacy number from a randomized trial. Filings, Phase 1, food-effect and status-only news go to Shorts. Bare 'What Is [drug]?' explainers (Lane P) are paused.
experiments.metric: Day-7 views and watch minutes against the GLP-1 long-form median (24 views, 45 min). Success: day-7 median of 50 views or more.
experiments.min_sample: n=4 qualifying videos made after 10-20 (2–4 weeks, depending on news).
experiments.result: In-window n=1: petrelintide (10-25) had 4 views at day 2; score it on 11-01. Elecoglipron (10-26) isn't logged and was a decoder, so it counts as Lane P, not C. Looking back at fresh next-gen results with a headline number: EloraTZP 575, Orforglipron 59, Survodutide 47, retatrutide 29 and 18, CagriSema 24. That's a signal, carried by one outlier.

experiments.name: Exp D: Shorts-to-long-form funnel with a verified link
experiments.hypothesis: A 20:00 funnel Short that asks a fresh question its live long-form answers, and carries a verified working link, will lift that long-form's daily views. Shorts get about 60 YouTube views each and currently send no measurable traffic to long-form.
experiments.change: Every 20:00 Short is a spin-off of a live long-form, rotating between that day's Lane C video, EloraTZP and Strength Training on Tirzepatide. Last spoken line: 'Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description.' No spoken title. The publisher automatically puts a verified '▶ Full breakdown' link on description line 1. Topic rules don't change.
experiments.metric: The target long-form's viewCount in the 3 days after the Short against the 3 days before. Once traffic sources are exported, also 'Shorts feed' and 'related video' traffic. Success: average lift of 10 or more views a day, or 50% or more over baseline.
experiments.min_sample: n=6 funnel Shorts with a verified working link. Shorts without a verified link are excluded.
experiments.result: Started 10-27; no data yet. Baseline: EloraTZP and Strength Training gained about 1–3 views a day before the experiment. Strength Training then jumped by about 11 a day (48 to 70 between day 9 and day 11), before the experiment, so use a per-video baseline.

owner_decisions: Turn on the impressions and CTR data. In the YouTube Reporting API, create a job for the channel reach report (metrics video_thumbnail_impressions and video_thumbnail_impressions_ctr). Add traffic source (insightTrafficSourceType) to the daily Analytics export. Why: 20 GLP-1 long-forms have a median of 24 views while viewers who click hold about 265 s. We can't tell whether thumbnails and titles fail (low CTR) or YouTube isn't showing the videos (low impressions). The SURMOUNT-5 long-form got 9 views while its Short got 163. Expected effect: in about 2–3 days we can retitle low-CTR long-forms and judge Exp D on real Shorts-feed traffic instead of view deltas.

Add end screens to all about 20 GLP-1 long-forms (Studio only, about 30 min). Use a best-for-viewer video, plus EloraTZP (575 views, 40% viewed, +7 subs) or Strength Training on Tirzepatide (70 views, still climbing), plus a subscribe element. Also create the playlists 'New GLP-1 Drug Decoded' and 'Life on GLP-1' and put every long-form in one. Why: long-forms bring nearly all the subscribers we can attribute (EloraTZP +7, Strength Training +1, How Long +1), and nothing currently chains one video into the next. Scripts now say 'the video on screen now', so they rely on end screens. Expected effect: more views per session and more watch time from the back catalogue at no production cost.

Set the related-video link on our top Shorts (Studio only, about 10 min): Retatrutide T2D (262) and bootleg Reta (199) → 'Did Retatrutide Beat Tirzepatide?'; Tirzepatide vs Semaglutide (163) → the SURMOUNT-5 long-form; Muscle (133) → Strength Training on Tirzepatide; Nausea (130) and Bones (231) → 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Side Effects and What Helps'. Why: 10,513 Shorts views in 90 days have sent no measurable traffic to long-form, and Shorts have no other clickable path. Expected effect: a first real Shorts-to-long-form path on our highest-reach videos, measurable once traffic sources are exported.

Fix the Shorts audio template. Set the default music level to the long-form level, and add an automatic loop that lowers the music by 3 dB and re-renders if masking is above 0.02, before the Editor-in-Chief sees it. Why: 5 of 21 Shorts were dropped this week for masking at 0.034–0.039, while all 14 long-forms mixed at 0.003–0.018. Two of the drops were retatrutide news, our top Shorts topic (peaks of 262 and 199). Expected effect: about 5 more Shorts a week, about 300 YouTube and 150+ Instagram views, and fewer wasted fact-check cycles.

Stop the daily 17:30 carousel, or cut it to 2 a week. Use the freed slot and Claude usage to re-render held Shorts the same day and to run a second QA pass on the long-form thumbnail and chapters. Why: about 35 carousels have reached 0–4 each (proven), and they add about 50 QA findings to the queue. Expected effect: no loss of reach, and a production slot back for the work that moves long-form watch time.
